title: Console backend: add rollout status aggregation endpoint (stages + gate summaries)
author: Felix Schneider
description: Summary: This PR adds a new console-backend endpoint that aggregates staged rollout status for Dedicated pools. It merges control-plane rollout plan data (stages/gates), gate-evaluator results, and audit/approval events into a single response optimized for the Console stage list + stage detail views. Motivation: The Console currently has to fan out to multiple services (control plane, evaluator, audit log) and stitch together stage state client-side, which is both slow and error-prone (race conditions between evaluator ticks and approvals). A single aggregation endpoint also lets us consistently implement the stage state machine and "fail safe" behavior (missing/late metrics => HOLD) and enforce cardinality limits for gate details. What’s included: (1) GET rollout status endpoint: GET /console/v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}/status returns current plan version, active stage, per-stage computed state, and per-gate evaluation summaries. (2) Stage state machine (server-side): Computes per-stage state from (a) plan definition, (b) current traffic weights from control plane policy snapshot, (c) approval events, and (d) latest gate evaluations. States: PENDING, RUNNING, HOLD, FAILED, COMPLETED, ABORTED, ROLLED_BACK (see docs string in StageStateMachine). (3) Gate evaluation summaries: For each gate, we return latest result (PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN), evaluation window, sample size, metrics freshness, and a normalized “reason” string for UI display. Missing metrics or evaluator lag beyond the tolerance automatically yields UNKNOWN + stage HOLD (matches ADR-027 direction). (4) Caching + load-shedding: Adds a short-lived cache (2s default) keyed by (tenant_id, pool_id, rollout_id, plan_version) to avoid hammering evaluator/audit services during UI polling. Also implements bounded fanout and timeouts; if evaluator is slow we still return stage state as HOLD with a degraded_reason. (5) Observability: Adds console-backend metrics for aggregation latency (p50/p95), upstream errors per dependency, and a counter for "hold_due_to_missing_metrics". Related: Linear ENG-5126 (Console backend workflows/APIs), PM-419 (stage definition UX + API contract). Notes/Limitations: - This endpoint is read-only and does not change rollout progression logic (advancement/hold/rollback is still owned by control plane + evaluator). - For v1 we only surface the latest evaluation per gate (no time-series). UI can link to dashboards for deep dives. - Approval event pagination is not exposed here; we only surface last approval/hold/abort event per stage for the stage list view. Example response fields (illustrative): plan_version=7; active_stage_id=stage-2; stages[].state=HOLD; stages[].gates[].summary='p95_latency exceeded threshold for 2/3 eval windows'; stages[].gates[].result=FAIL; stages[].last_event='AUTO_HOLD by gate-evaluator (missing_metrics=false)'. Testing: - Unit tests for state machine transitions (approvals vs evaluator tick ordering, missing metrics => HOLD). - Contract tests with control-plane stubs for plan_version mismatches. - Load test in staging with 1Hz polling across 50 pools; cache reduces upstream calls ~85%.

console-backend: add StageStateMachine with deterministic transitions

review_conversation:
Chloe Martin (review): The API shape looks good for the stage list. Two asks: (1) please make sure we never return RUNNING if any required gate is UNKNOWN due to missing metrics; UI will otherwise show green while evaluator is degraded. (2) Can we include a single top-level "degraded" indicator so the UI can show a banner?

Felix Schneider (author): Good call. I updated StageStateMachine so UNKNOWN for required gates forces stage to HOLD and adds degraded_reason="missing_metrics" or "evaluator_lag" depending on inputs. I also added top-level degraded=true + degraded_dependencies[] (strings) for banner use.

Ethan Park (review): Plan version handling: what happens if the plan changed while the console is polling? We’ve had bugs where UI shows stale stage states across plan updates.

Felix Schneider (author): Endpoint returns plan_version and will refuse to merge evaluator results from a different version. If versions mismatch, we return 409 with error_code=PLAN_VERSION_MISMATCH and include current_plan_version in the payload. The Console frontend already treats that as a refresh trigger (Kenji confirmed in DES-133 notes).

Logan Wright (review): Metric naming: please use the existing prefix console.rollouts.* and add dependency label but keep it low-cardinality (control_plane|evaluator|audit). Also ensure we don’t add tenant_id as a label.

Felix Schneider (author): Updated per guidance: dependency label is enum-only; tenant_id/pool_id are NOT labels. Added histogram console.rollouts.status_aggregate_latency_ms and counter console.rollouts.status_aggregate_upstream_errors_total{dependency}.

Allison Grant (review): Observability: can we log when we put a rollout into HOLD because evaluator is slow? That will help on-call correlate with evaluator issues.

Felix Schneider (author): Added structured log event rollout_status.degraded with fields: rollout_id, pool_id, degraded_reason, evaluator_last_seen_at, metrics_freshness_seconds.

Jordan Lee (review): Determinism question: Are we relying on "current weights" from routing policy snapshot? Those can lag a bit. Would prefer to use control-plane rollout state as the source of truth.

Felix Schneider (author): We’re using control-plane rollout state for active_stage + desired weights, and only using routing snapshot to show "observed" traffic distribution for UI (best effort). Updated naming to desired_weight/observed_weight to reduce confusion.

Chloe Martin (approval): Approved after the HOLD-on-UNKNOWN fix and the degraded banner addition.

CI note: Initial run failed on lint due to an unused import in gate_summary.ts; fixed in 9a3c0c1 and re-ran checks.
release_notes: Internal: Console backend now exposes a single endpoint to fetch Dedicated staged rollout status (stages + gate summaries) with fail-safe HOLD behavior when metrics are missing/degraded.
